newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Martin sees no more CPP premium increases.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin sees no more CPP premium increases.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin said on Friday that payments into the Canada Pension Plan will not be increased again.
"It's as high as the rate will go and it will not rise again," Martin told a business luncheon in Toronto.

One week ago, Martin introduced legislation to secure the future of the Canada Pension Plan by raising premium rates to 9.9 percent of insurable earnings over the next six years from 5.85 percent now.
The premiums are paid equally by employer and employee.
Opposition politicians have slammed the move, saying it amounts to one of the largest tax increases in Canadian history.
"Our major goal was to ensure the viability of the plan and that's what we have done," Martin told reporters on Friday. "That is 9.9 (percent) and it's not going to rise."
He said the previous arrangement would have eventually pushed premium rates up to 14 percent or further.
"What we have really done is provide a substantial premium reduction for young people."
